messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT ALERT: Multiple container restarts detected in cluster gpu-pool-4. Symptom: GPU OOM during prefill for long-context requests. Triggered 12x in last 2m. Paging @dave_oncall and ops rotation.

dave_oncall: Oncall here — joining. Any live customer impact?

carla_prodops: Support reports 3 customers seeing 500s and truncated streams. Partial failover to hosted fallback for some routes. Estimated affected requests ~0.6% of traffic but spikes on long-window endpoints.

ben_ml: Looking at traces — prefill phase memory spikes to ~100% VRAM then container restarts. Repro with long-window test (seq ~110k). KV-cache grows linearly, not being trimmed. Example stack from pod gpu-prefill-7:
```
E tensorflow/stream_executor/cuda/cuda_driver.cc:... CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY 
2026-03-17T18:20:13Z runtime.cpp:421 allocate: failed to alloc 1.2GB
ContainerExit: OOM_kill (signal 9)
```

alice_sre: Got it. I'm isolating node gpu-23 (suspected noisy neighbor). Planning: cordon + drain, scale down hotpool on that node, spin up temporary coldmodel workers on cpu-backed pool to absorb long-context. Executing now.

alice_sre: runbook commands:
```bash
kubectl cordon node/gpu-23
kubectl drain node/gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force
# scale hotpool to 0 on that node label
kubectl -n serving scale deployment hotpool-gpu --replicas=2
```

dave_oncall: Thanks. Immediate mitigation suggestions? Can we fallback long-window requests to quantized variant or smaller model?

ben_ml: Yes — push config to router to route "long_window" tag to redwood-mini-quant or to coldmodel. Also enable KV-cache trim on prefill: set PREFILL_KVCACHE_MAX=50MB for affected pool. Quick patch:
```json
{"router_rules": [{"match": {"metadata.context_tokens_gt": 50000}, "route_to": "redwood-mini-quant-v2"}]}
```

carla_prodops: I'll approve temporary throttling: reduce max_concurrent for long-window endpoints to 20. Also notify customer success for the 3 impacted accounts.

eve_support: Drafting customer note now: "We're investigating increased failures for very long inputs; we've implemented a mitigation (routing large requests to a lower-memory model) and will follow up with timelines. ETA next update in 30m." Want to add anything?

dave_oncall: Good. Add ETA + link to incident bridge. Also ask them to confirm whether any requests were retried client-side — might cause duplicate billing/latency.

alice_sre: Hot actions done: node cordoned/drained, hotpool scaled, router rule applied to route long-window to quant model, PREFILL_KVCACHE_MAX toggled. K8s events show evictions happening but no new OOMs on healthy nodes.

ben_ml: Observability: token-level metrics show prefill memory tail reduced ~85% on routed traffic. No further GPU OOMs in last 90s for affected pool.

incident-bot: UPDATE: incident status -> mitigated. Pager remains active for verification.

dave_oncall: Great work. Next steps: postmortem triage items: 1) make KV-cache trimming default for >50k tokens, 2) automatic fallback routing when prefill mem >80%, 3) noisy-neighbor detection alert. I'll create tickets.

eve_support: Customer note sent. Two customers acknowledged and appreciate fast action. One asked for SLA impact details — will loop in finance/CS for credits if needed.

alice_sre: Leaving watch on logs for 15m, will uncordon gpu-23 after confirmed stability and kernel reclaim verification.

dave_oncall: I'll keep timeline in incident doc and close once 30m stable. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

incident-bot: LOG: actions: router-rule-applied, node-cordon gpu-23, kvcache-param-updated, hotpool-scaled.

alice_sre: 15m checks green; no restarts in last 10m. Preparing uncordon in 5m.

dave_oncall: Closing pager soon. Final status: mitigated, customer impact limited, followups filed.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) at 3033337940."
